citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
The five IACUC approved protocols that were reviewed during today’s inspection did not contain a rationale for the
appropriateness of the species being used nor the number of animals to be used. IACUC approved protocols VETT 1010,
VETT 1600, VETT 2020, VETT 2100 and VETT 2500 simply stated the species and number of animals to be used. The
protocols did not provide a clear rationale for the appropriateness of the species or how the number of animals used were
calculated.
Providing a rationale for the species of animal as well as the number of animals to be used allows the IACUC to conduct a
thorough review of the use of animals within the research project and to ensure the proposed activities are in accordance
with the Animal Welfare Act. The facility must ensure that a proposal to conduct an activity involving animals, or to make a
significant change in an ongoing activity involving animals, must contain a rationale for involving animals, and for the
appropriateness of the species and numbers of animals to be used.
Correct by November 8th, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Additional Inspectors:
Eric Irvin, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
